arxiv-2102-09689.title: Do NHL goalies get hot in the playoffs? A multilevel logistic regression analysis
arxiv-2102-09689.creator: Likang Ding, Ivor Cribben, Armann Ingolfsson, Monica Tran
arxiv-2102-09689.description: Abstract The hot-hand theory posits that an athlete who has performed well in the recent past performs better in the present. We use multilevel logistic regression to test this theory for National Hockey League playoff goaltenders, controlling for a variety of shot-related and game-related characteristics. Our data consists of 48,431 48,431 shots for 93 goaltenders in the 2008–2016 playoffs.

arxiv-2202-10271.title: Radiation Hard 3D Silicon Pixel Sensors for use in the ATLAS Detector at the HL-LHC
arxiv-2202-10271.creator: A. Rummler
arxiv-2202-10271.description: Abstract The High Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC) upgrade requires the planned Inner Tracker (ITk) of the ATLAS detector to tolerate extremely high radiation doses. Specifically, the innermost parts of the pixel system will have to withstand radiation fluences above 1 × 10 16 1\times 10^{16} n e ​ q ​ c ​ m − 2 n_{eq}cm^{-2} .

arxiv-2205-13440.title: The Neuro-Symbolic Brain
arxiv-2205-13440.creator: Robert Lizée
arxiv-2205-13440.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Robert Lizée. Neural networks promote a distributed representation with no clear place for symbols. Despite this, we propose that symbols are manufactured simply by training a sparse random noise as a self-sustaining attractor in a feedback spiking neural network. This way, we can generate many of what we shall call prime attractors, and the networks that support them are like registers holding a symbolic value, and we call them registers. Like symbols, prime attractors are atomic and devoid of any internal structure.

arxiv-2206-14833.title: Doubly Charged Higgs Boson Production at Hadron Colliders II: A Zee-Babu Case Study
arxiv-2206-14833.creator: Richard Ruiz
arxiv-2206-14833.description: Abstract Motivated by searches for so-called leptonic scalars at the LHC and the recent measurement of the W W boson’s mass at the Tevatron, we revisit the phenomenology of the Zee-Babu model for neutrino masses and the ability to differentiate it from the Type II Seesaw model at the LHC.

arxiv-2301-02186.title: Inferring the impact of feedback on the matter distribution using the Sunyaev Zel’dovich effect: Insights from CAMELS simulations and ACT+DES data Inferring the impact of feedback on the matter distribution using the Sunyaev Zel’dovich effect: Insights from CAMELS simulations and ACT+DES data – 15
arxiv-2301-02186.creator: Shivam Pandey, Kai Lehman, Eric J. Baxter, Yueying Ni, Daniel Anglés-Alcázar, Shy Genel, Francisco Villaescusa-Navarro, Ana Maria Delgado, Tiziana di Matteo
arxiv-2301-02186.description: Abstract Feedback from active galactic nuclei and stellar processes changes the matter distribution on small scales, leading to significant systematic uncertainty in weak lensing constraints on cosmology. We investigate how the observable properties of group-scale halos can constrain feedback’s impact on the matter distribution using Cosmology and Astrophysics with MachinE Learning Simulations (CAMELS).

arxiv-2406-13302.title: SituationalLLM: Proactive language models with scene awareness for dynamic, contextual task guidance
arxiv-2406-13302.creator: Muhammad Saif Ullah Khan, Muhammad Zeshan Afzal, Didier Stricker
arxiv-2406-13302.description: Abstract Background. Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable success in text-based reasoning tasks but struggle to provide actionable guidance in real-world physical environments. This limitation arises from their lack of situational awareness—an inability to recognize gaps in their understanding of a user’s physical context, leading to unreliable and overly generic instructions.

arxiv-2406-14224.title: Cellular Automata model for period- n n synchronization: A new universality class.
arxiv-2406-14224.creator: Divya D. Joshi & Prashant M. Gade
arxiv-2406-14224.description: Abstract There are few known universality classes of absorbing phase transitions in one dimension and most models fall in the well-known directed percolation (DP) class. Synchronization is a transition to an absorbing state and this transition is often DP class. With local coupling, the transition is often to a fixed point state.

arxiv-2408-02492.title: Bargaining via Weber’s law
arxiv-2408-02492.creator: V.G. Bardakhchyan 1,2) and A.E. Allahverdyan 1,2)
arxiv-2408-02492.description: Abstract We solve the two-player bargaining problem employing Weber’s law in psychophysics, which is applied to the perception of utility changes. Using this law, the players define the jointly acceptable range of utilities on the Pareto line, which narrows down the range of possible solutions. Choosing a unique solution can be achieved by applying the Weber approach iteratively.

arxiv-2408-09585.title: On the Necessity of World Knowledge for Mitigating Missing Labels in Extreme Classification
arxiv-2408-09585.creator: Jatin Prakash, Anirudh Buvanesh, Bishal Santra, Deepak Saini, Sachin Yadav, Jian Jiao, Yashoteja Prabhu, Amit Sharma, Manik Varma
arxiv-2408-09585.description: Abstract . Extreme Classification (XC) aims to map a query to the most relevant documents from a very large document set. XC algorithms used in real-world applications learn this mapping from datasets curated from implicit feedback, such as user clicks. However, these datasets inevitably suffer from missing labels.

arxiv-2501-06823.title: MEXA-CTP: Mode Experts Cross-Attention for Clinical Trial Outcome Prediction
arxiv-2501-06823.creator: Yiqing Zhang, Xiaozhong Liu, Fabricio Murai
arxiv-2501-06823.description: Abstract Clinical trials are the gold standard for assessing the effectiveness and safety of drugs for treating diseases. Given the vast design space of drug molecules, elevated financial cost, and multi-year timeline of these trials, research on clinical trial outcome prediction has gained immense traction.

arxiv-2504-01478.title: Chemical Components in the Virgo Overdensity and Hercules-Aquila Cloud: hints of more than one merger event in GSE-like debris
arxiv-2504-01478.creator: Haoyang Liu, Cuihua Du, Thomas Donlon II, Mingji Deng
arxiv-2504-01478.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Haoyang Liu, Cuihua Du, Thomas Donlon II, Mingji Deng. Using elemental abundances for 1.26 million K giants in the LAMOST DR8 value-added catalog, we analyze the chemical abundances of the Virgo Overdensity (VOD) and Hercules-Aquila Cloud (HAC). We find two distinct chemical populations in both overdensities, which is in disagreement with the mainstream hypothesis that both overdensities are composed of materials from a single merger event, namely Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus (GSE).

arxiv-2510-16763.title: Bilateralist base-extension semantics with incompatible proofs and refutations
arxiv-2510-16763.creator: Victor Barroso-Nascimento, Maria Osório Costa, Elaine Pimentel
arxiv-2510-16763.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Victor Barroso-Nascimento, Maria Osório Costa, Elaine Pimentel. Logical bilateralism challenges traditional concepts of logic by treating assertion and denial as independent yet opposed acts. While initially devised to justify classical logic, its constructive variants show that both acts admit intuitionistic interpretations. This paper presents a bilateral system where a formula cannot be both provable and refutable without contradiction, offering a framework for modelling epistemic entities, such as mathematical proofs and refutations, that exclude inconsistency.

arxiv-2512-01365.title: Modeling Wavelet Transformed Quantum Support Vector for Network Intrusion Detection
arxiv-2512-01365.creator: Swati Kumari, Shiva Raj Pokhrel, Swathi Chandrasekhar, Navneet Singh, Hridoy Sankar Dutta, Adnan Anwar, Sutharshan Rajasegarar, Robin Doss
arxiv-2512-01365.description: Abstract Network traffic anomaly detection is a critical cybersecurity challenge requiring robust solutions for complex Internet of Things (IoT) environments. We present a novel hybrid quantum-classical framework integrating an enhanced Quantum Support Vector Machine (QSVM) with the Quantum Haar Wavelet Packet Transform (QWPT) for superior anomaly classification under realistic noisy intermediate-scale Quantum conditions.

Ho, Taku Fukuzawa, Hikaru Koga, Ken Ohmine, Hiroki Kawauchi, Masaru Muraoka, Yuri Ikuta, Garvita Gupta, Momoko Okuda, Ichio Onami, Miho Ayabe, Akira Takeiri, Hideyuki Konishi, Yui Sugawara, Shoko Usami, Eriko Ito, Norihito Shibahara, Kazuhisa Ozeki, Yukiko Wada, Ayano Hirako, Noriyuki Ta

This makes treatment compliance burdensome for patients.MethodsScreening was performed to identify anti-C1s antibodies specific for the CUB domain of C1s with CP neutralising function.

pmc-12662779.title: Patient Experiences of the Biopsychosocial Impact of Guillain-Barré Syndrome: A Scoping Review
pmc-12662779.creator: Vera Susanti, Yanny Trisyani, Aan Nuraeni
pmc-12662779.description: BackgroundGuillain-Barré Syndrome (GBS) is an acute autoimmune disorder of the peripheral nervous system that can lead to muscle weakness, respiratory failure, and long-term disability. While clinical aspects have been widely studied, evidence on the biopsychosocial-spiritual impacts among adults remains limited.

pmc-12751194.title: Effects of inspiratory muscle training on physical fitness in cystic fibrosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-12751194.creator: Aydan Asli Aksel-Uylar, Ceyhun Topcuoglu, Melda Saglam, Naciye Vardar-Yagli
pmc-12751194.description: BackgroundCystic fibrosis (CF) is a multisystem disease primarily affecting the lungs. It impacts physical fitness due to increased bronchial secretions and exercise intolerance. Inspiratory muscle training (IMT) is recommended as a pulmonary rehabilitation approach. Therefore, we aimed to examine the effect of inspiratory muscle training on health-related physical fitness in CF.

pmc-13021588.title: How recreational therapies impact physiological and psychosocial outcomes in cancer patients: a review
pmc-13021588.creator: Marika D’Oria, Calogero Casà, Cristina Cenci, Domenico Fusco, Beatrice Di Capua, Edoardo Vergani, Laura Monti, Anna Cardillo, Francesco Miccichè, Emilio Bria, Luca Tagliaferri, Maria Antonietta Gambacorta, Giampaolo Tortora, Vincenzo Valentini
pmc-13021588.description: Recreational Therapies (RecT) (e.g., art, dance, music, yoga, aromatherapy, Virtual Reality) are non-invasive interventions capable of enhancing the biopsychosocial wellbeing in patients, targeted to regenerate the existential dimensions of illness experience. While widely appreciated for their positive impact on quality of life, the specific biological and psychological mechanisms through which RecT exert their benefits remain underexplored in oncology.

pmc-13347750.title: Unveiling the Functional Role of KIF21B in Microglia Inflammatory Response
pmc-13347750.creator: Danny Ganchala, Alvaro Bautista‐Abad, Daniel Pinto‐Benito, Julia Simon‐Areces, Daniela Grassi, Francesco Paolo Ulloa Severino, Maria‐Angeles Arevalo
pmc-13347750.description: Microglia are brain immune cells that maintain homeostasis and respond to injury, changing cell morphology to drive inflammation, migration, and phagocytosis. This study examined the role of the kinesin KIF21B in microglial activation, demonstrating for the first time its expression in microglial cells in two in vivo neuroinflammatory models: TBI (focal inflammation) and LPS administration (diffuse inflammation).

pmc-13380531.title: Correlation of type 3 secretion system genes with antimicrobial resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa: A unique clinical signature
pmc-13380531.creator: Farkhanda Afaque, Aliya Hayat, Somia Gul, Ayaz Ahmed, Mahmooda Kazmi
pmc-13380531.description: ObjectivesPseudomonas aeruginosa is a well-known opportunistic pathogen with intrinsic multidrug resistance, extensive drug resistance, and multiple virulence factors, making hospital-acquired infections therapy resistant. The type 3 secretion system (T3SS) and its four effector proteins, i.e., ExoS, ExoT, ExoU, and ExoY, have invasive and cytotoxic effects that lead to host cell death.

pmc-13381587.title: Bio-inspired antioxidant stabilization for efficient tin-lead and all-perovskite tandem solar cells
pmc-13381587.creator: Yiting Jiang, Tingfeng Lei, Chengda Ge, Yidan An, Nan Zhang, Yunfan Wang, Lingyi Ke, Zhiqiang Guan, Chun-To Wong, Danning Lyu, Zhihui Liu, Jingdong Luo, Sai-Wing Tsang, Zaiwei Wang, Alex K.-Y. Jen, Hin-Lap Yip
pmc-13381587.description: The development of high-performance narrow-bandgap tin-lead (Sn-Pb) perovskite solar cells (PSCs) is fundamental to surpassing the Shockley-Queisser limit via all-perovskite tandem configurations. Nevertheless, the vulnerability of Sn2+ to oxidation in Sn-Pb perovskite films and devices remains a formidable obstacle to achieving superior film quality and competitive power conversion efficiency (PCE).

pmc-13429539.title: Enhancing Postoperative Outcomes After Metabolic Bariatric Surgery: a Pilot Study of Inhibitory Control Training, Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation and Psychosocial Aftercare
pmc-13429539.creator: Sarah Alica Rösch, Carsten Thiele, Therese Reinstaller, Tino Zähle, Kathrin Schag, Katrin Giel, Christian Plewnia, Johann Steiner, Florian Junne, Susanne Vogt
pmc-13429539.description: IntroductionHeightened food-specific impulsivity, associated with prefrontal cortex hypoactivity, may impair outcomes following metabolic bariatric surgery (MBS). This pilot study examined the feasibility of transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) targeting the right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) combined with an individualized food-specific inhibitory control training addressing behavioral impulsivity alongside psychosocial follow-up (FU) care to support early postoperative lifestyle adaptation.

uslaw-usc-t16-s667.title: 16 U.S.C. § 667 — Game management supply depots; appropriations
uslaw-usc-t16-s667.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t16-s667.description: United States Code, Title 16 (Conservation); Chapter 5A (Protection And Conservation Of Wildlife); Subchapter I (Game, Fur-Bearing Animals, And Fish). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Appropriations made for the administration, protection, maintenance, control, improvements, and development of wildlife sanctuaries, reservations, and refuges under the control of the Secretary of the Interior shall be available for the purchase, transportation, and handling of supplies.
